result: I'd make it so that people could instinctively feel the long-term, cascading consequences of their actions on others and the natural world—not as abstract data or future projections, but as a visceral, immediate awareness, like pain or hunger. It wouldn't eliminate conflict or guarantee agreement, but it would make indifference, exploitation, and short-term extraction feel as untenable as burning your own hand. Economics, policy, and daily decisions would naturally align with stewardship and reciprocity, simply because causing distant or delayed harm would register on the nervous system of culture itself.
